entry.title: Get the audio bundle out of the critical path, and teach 没
entry.content:
Get the audio bundle out of the critical path, and teach 没

v1.3.0. Three things, from a look at what was actually costing the most.

A first visit downloaded 1.33 MB before anything drew, and 859 KB of that was
js/audio.js — base64 speech, loaded as a blocking script, that nothing needs in
the first second. app.js fetches it after the first render now. Everything that
reads a clip already guarded on HQ_AUDIO existing, so the seconds before it
lands degrade to the system voice rather than to an error.

That had a trap in it. The unlock listeners were bound with {once: true}, and a
once listener is spent even on a call that returns early — so a click landing
before the bundle arrived would have burned the only chance to unlock the audio
element and left the whole visit silent. They stay armed now, at the cost of an
early return per click. Verified: an early click no longer consumes the unlock,
and a later one still works.

Then a real curriculum hole. 55 of 348 example sentences could not be used as
reading material because they contained a character the library never taught,
and the worst of them was 没 — 没有 is among the commonest things anyone says in
Chinese and it simply wasn't there. Nor 哪 which, nor 怎 how, nor 吧.

Sixteen characters go in where they belong rather than appended to the end: 没
哪 怎 吧 into Sprout with the other negation and question words, 第 金 into
Explorer with money and numbers, 儿 孩 先 岁 间 气 into Everyday with people and
time, 京 床 桌 力 into The World. Records key on the character rather than its
index, so inserting mid-curriculum is safe and only the STAGES end values move.
Blocked sentences fell from 55 to 30; readable words rose to 622. 364
characters, 575 clips, every component claim and stroke order still checks out.

And the README's opening section still told a future session to publish to a
Claude Artifact that has been stale for a dozen versions, with no mention of the
repo, the SSH remote, or the version bump that keeps a push from being invisible.
It documents how this actually ships now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Add a flashcard deck of words you can already read
entry.content:
Add a flashcard deck of words you can already read

Characters are only half of reading: knowing 大 and 人 separately does not get
you 大人. A third deck collects every multi-character word in the library whose
characters are all already yours, and fills itself as you go — 78 words at 72
characters, 212 at 140.

Words are listed under each character they contain, so they are deduplicated,
and ordered by the last character to fall into place. Newest first means the
deck opens on the combinations you have only just become able to read rather
than on 一个 forever.

The back names the parts — 大 big + 人 person — because seeing what a word is
made of is the thing that makes it stick. Deck entries are now either a
character (a plain string) or a word (its triple), and flashFace() reduces
either to the same shape so the renderer doesn't branch. Word cards carry no
tone glyph: the mark draws a single contour, and 大人 has two syllables with two
different ones, so one shape would be a lie.

Shortening a meaning to fit needed more care than splitting on the first
punctuation mark. Fourteen characters are pure grammar and glossed entirely
inside brackets — 们 is "(plural marker for people)" — which that rule shortens
to nothing, and 得 "(links verb to description); to obtain" shortened to a
fragment with a stray bracket. shortMeaning() prefers what follows a leading
parenthetical and falls back to its contents; all 348 now gloss cleanly.

v1.2.0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Placement credits are not "learned today"
entry.content:
Placement credits are not "learned today"

Being placed at 69 characters filled the Learned today strip with all 69 and
pointed the whole practice list at them: recognise these 69, pronounce these
69, write out these 69. The intended day one — five new characters — was buried
under a day's work nobody asked for.

Placement credits land today, so ensure() stamps `first` with today's date
whichever way a character arrives, and learnedToday() had no way to tell them
apart. It now filters on `placed`, which is exactly the flag that separates
"credited this morning" from "sat down and learnt it this morning".

Miss three of your first 72 and Today now shows those three plus the next two
in the library — five characters, the same first session everybody gets. That
half needed no change: nextNew() walks the curriculum in order and skips what
you know, so the gaps you left come first by construction.

Every task is scoped to those five except Read them in context, which tops up
from characters you already read. A character learnt an hour ago usually has no
sentence you can read yet — every other glyph in it is still unknown — so
scoping reading strictly to today left that row locked most days. It is also
the one task where the older characters are the point: reading in context means
reading the context, and the context is everything you already know. Ticking
still requires only today's characters, so the inference in renderDone keeps
comparing like with like.

v1.1.1.

entry.title: Fix three audio bugs, duplicate quiz options, and give the word of th…
entry.content:
Fix three audio bugs, duplicate quiz options, and give the word of the week something to recall

v1.1.0.

Tapping a word in "Words you'll meet it in" got worse the longer you browsed:
it would play only the first character, then stop speaking at all. bindCard
attaches its click handler to #svBody, which lives for the whole session while
only its innerHTML is swapped — so every card opened stacked another listener.
The second card fired each click twice, the third three times, and since every
call starts by cancelling the phrase the last one just began, they cancelled
each other. Bind once and replace the handler instead of piling one on.

Separately, 现金 was silent. Clips were generated for the 348 taught characters
only, but example words use characters from outside the curriculum — 金 in 现金,
第 in 第一, 儿 in 女儿, 225 of them across 121 words. One missing clip made
sayPhrase give up on the whole word and fall through to the system voice, which
says nothing on a machine with no Chinese voice. make-audio.mjs now records
every character the app can be asked to say, from words, sentences, the menu
and the interest lists as well as the curriculum: 573 clips, 4.0 MB. A smoke
check walks the data and fails if anything speakable has no clip. sayPhrase
also steps over a gap rather than stopping at one, so a bundle that has drifted
from the data is imperfect rather than mute.

And a listening drill could play the wrong character. say() detached the phrase
handler but left phraseTimer running, so a step queued by the previous card
still fired and played its own character over the top — being marked wrong for
answering what you actually heard. say() now cancels the phrase properly, and
renderStep silences the previous card on the way in.

Quiz options were only guaranteed distinct from the answer, not from each
other, and characters share readings: 个 could be offered shì, shì, shì, gè.
optionSet() deduplicates on the value the learner compares. Twenty thousand
generated drills across all five multiple-choice kinds now produce no duplicate
and always contain the answer.

The word of the week no longer prints its own meaning. Working out 音乐 from 音
and 乐 was the point, and the answer was sitting underneath — with a note that
names the characters it explains, which forty of them do. Meaning and note are
behind a reveal now, and nine notes that merely restated the English meaning
were rewritten to say something worth reading.

entry.title: Version the app so a cached copy can be told from a stale deploy
entry.content:
Version the app so a cached copy can be told from a stale deploy

Twice now a push has been live and invisible at the same time — once for the
save icon, once for the placement quiz's number keys. Both times the deploy was
already correct and the browser was serving a cached js/app.js, and there was
no way to tell that from the app itself.

Every local asset now carries ?v=<version>, so the URL changes when the version
does and the fetch is forced. The version lives in index.html and nowhere else:
once in an inline script for the app to read, once in each asset's query
string. Deliberately not in a .js file — a cached script asked what version it
is would always give the reassuring answer. index.html has no query string of
its own and is the file browsers reliably revalidate.

It shows in Settings, with a line about what a mismatch means, and at the foot
of Record.

tools/version.mjs bumps it: major/minor/patch or an explicit number, rewriting
all six stamps and setting the date. Run bare it reports the current version
and whether the stamps agree. A smoke check fails if the declared version and
the stamps ever diverge, or if a local asset is added without one — a half-done
bump is worse than no version at all, because the number on screen would claim
a refresh that never happened.

Starting at 1.0.0: the first version that can be identified from outside.

entry.title: Keyboard control for the placement quiz
entry.content:
Keyboard control for the placement quiz

1-4 to answer, space for "I don't know this one", enter to start from the
result screen — the same keys the study session already uses. The numbers are
drawn in the corner of each option so the character stays optically centred.

A question now latches the moment it is answered. The options are disabled on
the way out but the skip button is not, so a held space counted one miss per
key repeat: four presses ended the quiz three characters early, and the reveal
delay made that easy to do by accident rather than by mashing. The latch also
swallows number keys during the reveal, which could otherwise answer the
question underneath before it had rendered.

entry.title: Placement credits what it asked, and never builds a day-one backlog
entry.content:
Placement credits what it asked, and never builds a day-one backlog

Being placed at 100 characters meant opening the app to sixty-odd cards on day
one — a mixture of characters you knew cold and characters you had never seen.
That is the worst possible first session: too long, and too uneven to be either
satisfying or useful. It was also still guessing, since five characters stood
for twenty and most of a credited range was never shown.

The quiz now walks every character in curriculum order and stops once you have
missed more than three. A character is credited if and only if you answered it
correctly. Nothing is sampled and nothing is inferred.

And credit stopped meaning homework. A credited character goes into the library
as known — it counts for tier progress, Go deeper draws it, it inks itself in
sentences and vocabulary, exactly as if it had been learnt in an earlier
session. What it does not do is land in tomorrow's queue: its first review sits
twelve days out, fanned across twenty-four more. The exception is the tail, the
last twelve you got right before you started missing, which are the shakiest
things you know because you were at the edge of your range — those come back
within the week at a lower level. That is the refresher, without the backlog.

Day one after placement is now the day one everybody gets: five new characters,
zero reviews, starting at the first character you actually missed. Verified end
to end — 60 credited, 0 due, "5 new and 0 reviews still waiting".

The walk is exhaustive, so "That's enough — start me here" appears after twelve
questions and finishes on the spot, keeping everything answered so far.

Also in this change:

Buttons that set no background of their own kept the user agent's light grey,
which is invisible under light text in dark mode. That is what hid the
unhighlighted half of every word in "Words you'll meet it in". The global reset
now clears it.

Finishing the day's list, or every character in every Go deeper mode, gets a
seal stamp, falling petals and five notes of a pentatonic scale — synthesised
rather than bundled, because js/audio.js already demonstrated how a shipped
asset goes missing. Both are latched, and the Go deeper latch clears when a new
character makes the library incomplete so it can be earned again.

Word of the week now knows what week it is. Nine festivals from 春节 to
Christmas take precedence over the interest pool when one falls in the current
ISO week. Lunar dates are tabled per year rather than computed — a year outside
the table declines to fire instead of guessing. Festival history is never
wiped, so six Christmases run without repeating.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Placement decides where to start, not what you know
entry.content:
Placement decides where to start, not what you know

The quiz samples — five characters stand for twenty — and then credited the
whole range at PLACED_LVL, including the characters it had never actually
shown. Placed at 100 after 30 questions, that is 76 characters assumed on the
strength of their neighbours and 24 with any evidence behind them, stored
identically and indistinguishable afterwards.

Those are two different claims and they are now credited differently. A
character the quiz asked and you answered goes in at PLACED_LVL with its first
review fanned over PLACED_SPREAD days. One it never asked goes in at level 0,
flagged `unchecked`, fanned wider over CHECK_SPREAD. Level 0 is the bottom of
the ladder, so the first time an unchecked character comes up it is an ordinary
recognition card: right and it climbs like anything else, wrong and it is
taught properly from there. grade() clears the flag either way, because the
question has been settled.

So nothing is assumed permanently — it is verified lazily, through the review
machinery that already exists, rather than by making someone answer 348
questions before they start. In testing a single session settled 74 of 76.

The count is visible rather than silent: Today carries an Unchecked pill while
any remain, and a character card credited this way says so on its face. The
result screen no longer claims "you already read about 100 characters" — it
reports what was asked, what was not, and what happens to the difference, and
says outright that the quiz only decides where to start.

entry.title: Group the library into three tiers, and gate the ones you haven't rea…
entry.content:
Group the library into three tiers, and gate the ones you haven't reached

The Library laid all 348 characters out in one sheet. That did two bad things:
it made a beginner scroll past hundreds they had no business opening yet, and
it let them open one anyway — out of order, without any of the parts it is
built from.

Three tiers now sit across the nine teaching stages, at the conventional
literacy milestones: 200 for signs, prices and the shape of a sentence, 500 for
most everyday writing, 1000 for roughly nine characters in ten on a page. The
Library groups by tier, each collapsible, with the tier you are actually in
left open and the rest shut — and a locked tier collapses to a single card
saying what would open it, rather than 150 grey squares. The Record ladder is
grouped the same way.

A tier opens at 80% of the tier before it, and of every tier before that, so a
gap early on can't be stepped over. unlockedCeiling() gates nextNew(), so a
session never deals a locked character; remainingNew(), so "study ahead" stops
promising characters the gate would refuse; and the Learn this one now button,
which becomes an explanation of which tier the character is in and what opens
it. The card itself still reads in full — etymology, mnemonic, words, sentence,
stroke order. It just isn't one to start on yet.

Two things deliberately reach past the gate. Placement credits beyond it,
because proving you read 300 characters is exactly what should open tier 2 —
and it does, with no special case, since the unlock is computed from what you
know. And the word of the week routinely uses characters far beyond your tier,
which is the point of it, and is safe because it is never a drill.

Tiers and stages don't line up — stage 7 straddles 200 — so each stage is filed
under whichever tier its midpoint falls in. Listing a straddling stage under
both tiers reads as a bug rather than as precision.

Also: tierNeeds() returns the first unfinished tier, which is the right gate but
the wrong sentence — it told someone on tier 1 that ninety more characters would
open Fluent, which the third door was never going to honour. tierGateNote() now
names the intermediate tier when the blocker isn't the one immediately before.

And the top-bar save button is a save icon rather than a download arrow.

entry.title: Auto-trackpad, placement quiz, interests, and a practice pool that ro…
entry.content:
Auto-trackpad, placement quiz, interests, and a practice pool that rotates

Four things, all about the app meeting the learner where they actually are.

Settings gains "Start the trackpad automatically": every writing box arms
itself as it appears rather than waiting for the 触控 button or T. Off by
default, because pointer lock hides the cursor and doing that unasked is
startling. It goes through padAuto(), which is allowed to fail — pointer lock
generally wants a user gesture and a card arriving on the auto-advance timer
hasn't got one, so a refusal is expected rather than exceptional. It sets
pad.quiet, which suppresses the "browser blocked pointer lock" note: an
automatic attempt the browser turns down is not an error anyone needs to read
about, and the manual button is still exactly where it was.

A placement quiz, offered once at the end of the tour, walks the curriculum in
order and finds where recognition gives out — five characters sampled across
each twenty positions, four right to credit the window and move on. Someone
who reads the first ~95 characters is placed at 100 after about thirty
questions. Questions are meaning-to-character, not the reverse: recognising 山
among four English words is easy to fake by elimination, picking it out of four
plausible characters is not, and the distractors come from within thirty
positions so they are of a piece. Credit is shallow on purpose — level 2,
flagged as placed, first reviews fanned across five days so a hundred
characters land as twenty a day rather than a wall, and nothing at all is due
on day one. placeAt() may only ever add: a character already in the record is
left strictly alone, or retaking after a month of study would knock it back to
level 2 and reset its due date, which is a silent partial reset dressed up as
a re-place.

Then a name and any number of interests, feeding one real word a week from
whatever you said you cared about — usually built from characters well past
where you have reached, with a line about where it comes from. Interests
deliberately do NOT reorder the curriculum: that order is load-bearing, 马 has
to arrive before 妈 and 吗 whoever you are, and letting a preference reshuffle
it would quietly break the thing that makes each character easier than the
last. The word of the week runs beside the curriculum instead, and is never
scheduled, graded, counted or added to the review queue — the moment it becomes
homework it stops doing its job.

And practice rounds rotate now. Sorting the whole library by weakness and
taking the top N stopped working once the library got big: the same forty were
always the weakest, so the same forty came round every time. Rounds are now 70%
from the last forty characters introduced and 30% reaching back into everything
older, and within either group what comes up is what has come up least —
records carry `shown` (times asked) beside `skills` (times right), and weakness
is only the tie-break. Ordering by weakness first pins a character you keep
missing to the front of the queue permanently, which is how you see 难 six
times in an evening. Over forty simulated rounds against two hundred
characters the split holds at exactly 70%, 160 distinct characters come up, and
no older character is asked more than three times.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Separate Go deeper from today's list, and add stage 9
entry.content:
Separate Go deeper from today's list, and add stage 9

Go deeper was styled as a second half of Today's practice, which framed it
wrongly. Today's list is scoped to the day's characters, finishable, and it
ticks; Go deeper is the whole library, unbounded, and can never be completed.
Given the same treatment, a fraction that never reaches its denominator reads
as failure rather than as work done.

It is no longer a .sheet. It sits on inked ground with no tick boxes, and its
reward is a count that only goes up: reps, tallied in 正 — five strokes, the
tally mark used across China and Japan, one stroke per rep, so a finished 正
is five and a row of them is the day's work at a glance. It was chosen over
stars or a growing tree because it is the genuine article rather than
decoration, and because the seedling-to-tree metaphor already belongs to the
stage ladder, where it means something else.

Reps live in days[k].extra and are sealed off from every other counter:
tallyExtra() fires only when session.practice is set and session.todo is not,
so a row from today's list never inflates them, and a rep never counts as a
character revised or ticks anything off. Smoke checks hold both directions.

Stage 9, 交流 Connect, adds 46 characters for what stages 1-8 left out: the
courtesy words, the vocabulary of thinking and remembering, language and
study, screens, and the shape of a working week. It closes some conspicuous
gaps — 谢谢 and 再见 were not previously writable — and lets the app teach its
own name, 汉字.

The block is ordered so nothing needs a part it hasn't met: 见 comes first and
视 and 觉 are built on it, 音 precedes 意, 自 precedes 息, 己 precedes 记. Every
comp claim is validated against Make Me a Hanzi; stroke data and speech clips
are regenerated for all 348. The tour's character count now comes from the
data rather than being typed in, since it was already stale once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Fix silent audio, buried saving, a reset that didn't, and counters th…
entry.content:
Fix silent audio, buried saving, a reset that didn't, and counters that miscounted

Four things reported after publishing to GitHub, all of which turned out to be
the app failing quietly rather than failing loudly.

Audio was silent because js/audio.js was in .gitignore, so anything served
from a clone got a 404 for it — and a missing <script> fails with nothing in
the console. The bundle is committed now. It is macOS `say` output, so the
licensing caveat the ignore rule was protecting is spelled out in the README
instead of enforced by making the app mute. When the bundle genuinely isn't
loaded, Settings now says so and gives the command to regenerate it.

Reset did nothing at all in the published artifact. Every destructive action
was guarded by `if (!confirm(...)) return;`, and a sandbox without allow-modals
makes confirm() return false immediately — no dialog, no error, no console
message — so the guard silently became `return;`. This also disabled Restore
and made it impossible to close a session part-way through. Replaced with
askConfirm(), an in-page dialog that works the same in a frame, a tab and on
Pages, and that names what is about to be lost.

Reset was also incomplete where it did run: Object.assign(state, blank()) only
overwrites the keys blank() declares, so menuPick and lastBackup outlived it,
and the practice diary (IndexedDB), the exercise book on screen and the tour
were never touched at all. resetProgress() replaces the binding outright and
the caller clears the other three. A smoke check asserts no key outlives a
reset so this can't rot as fields are added.

Saving progress was three screens deep under Settings, and on an ordinary page
its only path was the artifact host's downloads capability, which doesn't
exist there — so it fell through to "copy this JSON out of a textarea". It is
now a top-bar button that does a real Blob download, and grows a gold dot once
there is progress worth losing and no saved copy.

The counters on Today disagreed about their own unit. "Reviewed today"
incremented per answer while sitting beside New and Due, which count
characters, so one character drilled four times read as four; it now counts
distinct characters, and the hero ring is measured the same way. Today's
practice omitted the learn row and silently dropped locked steps from the
denominator, so a five-row list read "3 of 3 done"; it now counts every
actionable step and reports locked ones separately.

Go deeper only moved on a character's third correct answer, so a whole round
of practice could change nothing on screen, and measured writing against every
character known — which it can never reach, since a character without stroke
data can't be drilled. The ring now fills with every clean pass, each mode is
measured against the characters it can actually ask about, and a segmented bar
shows the spread across nought, one, two and three passes. Record's Skills
panel uses the same maths, over characters known rather than the whole library.

Also fixed in passing: .pr-grid-3 was referenced in JS but never defined in
CSS, so Go deeper laid out as three of four columns and left a quarter of the
sheet empty; and the streak chip showed a cold 0 on first paint because
renderStreakChip() was never called at boot.

entry.title: Hanzi Quest: a practice notebook for reading Chinese
entry.content:
Hanzi Quest: a practice notebook for reading Chinese

302 characters across seven core stages plus a kitchen topic pack, taught in
an order where each one makes the next easier — 马 arrives just before 妈 and
吗, so the phonetic-compound principle lands on its own.

Every character carries real stroke-order animation, etymology separate from
the mnemonic, grammar tags, the words it lives in, and a sentence. Recognition,
pronunciation, recall and handwriting are tracked as four separate skills,
because they are separate knowledge.

Today is a finishable to-do list scoped to the day's characters. "Read a Menu"
teaches one character a day from a real restaurant menu that grows in
difficulty as you do. Writing works with mouse, finger or a pointer-locked
trackpad, and there's a blank 米字格 exercise book with a practice diary stored
as stroke vectors in IndexedDB.

Three checks guard the data:
  tools/smoke.mjs             contract, curriculum, scheduling, side quest
  tools/check-components.mjs  every "Built from" claim vs Make Me a Hanzi
  tools/check-strokes.mjs     every stroke, in order, vs upstream graphics
